Good to know Scheduling notes

Times and lunches

For overnight shifts, choose the following date for the end time. A split can be used as a lunch. U = unpaid lunch; P = paid lunch. Only unpaid lunches reduce paid hours.

Vietnam

Lunch is paid: 30 minutes for day shifts and 45 minutes for shifts starting between 10 PM and 6 AM Vietnam time. Night eligibility uses the entered start time. The night window includes 10 PM and ends before 6 AM.

New York

Morning lunch: 30 unpaid minutes when the shift works the entire 11 AM–2 PM window and lasts at least six hours. Schedule lunch within that window, no later than 1 PM. Evening/overnight lunch: 45 unpaid minutes halfway through shifts starting from 1 PM to before 6 AM and lasting more than six hours. A second 30-minute unpaid lunch is required between 5 PM and 7 PM when the schedule starts before 11 AM, ends after 7 PM, and works both full windows—even across a split. Paid 15-minute breaks still apply. Part-time staff have no exception. Lunch scheduling instructions apply to the entered local clock.

The guide’s detailed second-lunch section specifies 30 minutes; its opening summary says 20 minutes. The calculator follows the detailed 30-minute instruction.

US scheduling guidance

The supplied US guide uses California break and lunch requirements for all US states. New York has a separate policy button. All scheduled breaks are 15 minutes, and US lunches are unpaid.

The supplied state notes list an eight-hour daily maximum for Alaska, California, and Puerto Rico; no seven consecutive workdays for California, Illinois, Kentucky, Massachusetts, and New Hampshire; and lunch between 5 and 5.75 hours for California, Colorado, New Hampshire, North Dakota, and Washington, unless an HR waiver is sent and signed by the interpreter.

These are notes from the supplied internal guide, rather than extra checks in this calculator. Confirm current scheduling exceptions with HR or your LOM.

US lactation breaks

When a lactation break is added to a paid break, the guide calls for 10 additional paid minutes. Additional lactation breaks outside regular breaks are unpaid and require extending the schedule. These allowances are not included in the calculator totals.

US unscheduled breaks

For US agents only: unscheduled breaks require LOM approval and have a 20-minute maximum. The guide treats a break over 20 minutes, or one without LOM approval, as an absence. Ask whether approval was received.
